title: Access Control (ACL)

sections.heading: Key concepts
sections.content: An ACL (Access Control List) defines the requirements (role, condition, script) needed to perform an operation (create, read, write, delete) on a table or field. ServiceNow first evaluates table-level ACLs, then field-level ACLs for the same operation.

sections.heading: Roles and security
sections.content: If an ACL specifies no role and has neither a condition nor a script, it grants access to any authenticated user who reaches that ACL — a classic pitfall. The 'security_admin' role, combined with role elevation (Elevate Roles), is required to modify the ACLs themselves in most instances.

sections.heading: Types of ACLs
sections.content: There are table ACLs (record-level: create/read/write/delete), field ACLs (field-level, more restrictive than the table), and 'ui' or 'client_callable' level ACLs to secure specific scripts (e.g. Script Includes exposed to the client).

pieges: Believing that a Client Script enforces server-side security: real security is always enforced server-side via ACLs, never on the client alone.
Forgetting the evaluation order: a field ACL is never reached if the corresponding table ACL already fails.
Thinking that the admin role automatically bypasses all ACLs without explicit configuration ('Admin overrides').
